name: is_signed
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied registered schema: "aten::is_signed(Tensor self) -> bool". This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation contract, and tests must never be narrowed, removed or have reference behavior adapted to fit this one signature. All supplied registered schema strings: "aten::is_signed(Tensor self) -> bool". Semantics derived from the tests: is_signed is a dtype predicate that reads no stored element and returns a Python bool (not a tensor); it is True for the signed integer kinds (int8/int16/int32/int64) and for every float/complex kind (float16/bfloat16/float32/float64/complex32/complex64/complex128 and float8 variants), and False for bool and the unsigned integer kinds (uint8/uint16/uint32/uint64). The answer depends only on dtype, so strides, storage offset, memory layout (transposed, storage-offset view, expanded stride-0, channels_last, conj/neg views), sparse COO layout, meta device, zero-size shapes and NaN/Inf element contents do not change the result. Because the schema is unary with exactly one Tensor argument, a non-tensor argument, an extra second argument, and a quantized tensor (at::isSignedType has no quantized branch) are all rejected with RuntimeError/TypeError. No broadcast, scalar-operand, backward or value-range workload applies: the signature is unary and the bool result carries no autograd graph. The single ATen return is a bool scalar, so the definition exposes one logical output and no mutation or aliasing effects; the other registered signature forms remain covered by the original pytest.
